title: 1 Parking Poste de Secours, 19380 Albussac, France - Albussac grande cascade_
author: kaoss012
notes: Albussac 'grande cascade' (Correze, France), natural forest waterfall roar, Zoom H6, lossless 44.1k stereo. Rock-steady texture (LRA 0.7), dense low-mid roar with natural top to ~10 kHz, no voices/traffic/birds visible. Segment skips the recordist's fade-in (first ~14 s) and fade-out (last ~7 s).

title: QJCC+35 Saint-Mamet, France - Cascade de Sidonie
author: kaoss012
notes: Cascade de Sidonie near Luchon (Pyrenees, France), same recordist/kit (Zoom H6), lossless. Brighter, more open roar than Albussac; mid band level constant to +/-0.5 dB over the whole segment, LF (20-80 Hz) steady at ~-40 dB (falls rumble, not wind gusts). Fade-in/out excluded. Pair with falls-1 for variety.

title: Derrysallagh, Geevagh, Co. Sligo, Ireland - Babbling Stream
author: Benjamin Burns
notes: Babbling stream (Derrysallagh, Co. Sligo, Ireland), Zoom H1 held just above the water surface on a calm sunny day; lossless 44.1k. Very consistent close-up babble/trickle texture (LRA 0.7), energy 250 Hz-8 kHz, nothing below ~200 Hz (no wind rumble), no voices/vehicles. Caveat: H1 XY is fairly narrow (L/R corr 0.84) and the texture is even rather than 'gurgle-event' rich.

title: Unnamed Road, 76596 Forbach, Deutschland - Rote Lache - Black Forest, morning birds
author: avoelzing
notes: Rote Lache, Black Forest (Germany): forest morning ambience with several songbirds at medium/far distance, no water. Lossless 48k stereo. Traffic band (150-1000 Hz) is flat - no vehicle or aircraft swells; birdsong 2-9 kHz throughout. Caveats: quiet recording (-37 LUFS) with a steady sub-100 Hz rumble (wind/air) - a high-pass around 80-100 Hz is recommended; birds are fairly busy (spring morning)

title: Sherwood Forest - Wind in the Trees
author: rcarlberg
notes: Wind high in the tree canopy ('wash of white noise') on a clear day, gentle-to-moderate gusts swelling every 20-40 s, energy 250 Hz-3 kHz, no mic-wind rumble blobs in this segment (the two small LF bumps at 84 s and 228 s are excluded). Source is a 69-min 320 kbps MP3; the local file is the first 300 s of it (byte-range download), times are identical to the original. Faint insect ticks 3-5 kHz. Ca
